## Natural history notes

A small burrowing bug characterized by a dark oval body, strong digging legs, and two pale lines or bands that give it the “two-lined” appearance. In Florida, the Two-lined Burrowing Bug is found in sandy or loose soils in lawns, fields, gardens, roadsides, pine flatwoods, scrub edges, and other open or semi-open habitats with low vegetation. Adults and nymphs live at or below the soil surface, feeding by piercing plant roots, seeds, or underground plant parts, while also serving as prey for birds, lizards, spiders, ants, and other ground-foraging predators.
